en: Mayon Volcano in Albay has a permanent six-kilometer danger zone where people must not live or enter during eruptions.
Coastal towns in Eastern Visayas facing the Pacific Ocean must prepare for tsunamis after strong underwater earthquakes.
Living near the Pasig River in Manila requires boiling water or using filters to prevent waterborne diseases from pollution.
Wearing light-colored, loose cotton clothing helps children in Metro Manila stay cool and prevent heatstroke during the dry season.
Clearing stagnant water in tires around your home in Quezon City prevents mosquitoes from breeding and spreading dengue fever.
Hiking Mount Pulag in Benguet requires wearing thick jackets because temperatures can drop below freezing at its highest peak.
During heavy monsoon rains, residents near the Cagayan River must evacuate to higher ground to avoid dangerous flash floods.
Applying sunscreen with at least SPF 30 protects skin from harmful ultraviolet rays while swimming in El Nido, Palawan.
Houses built directly above the Valley Fault System in Metro Manila are at high risk of collapsing during strong earthquakes.
Wearing an N95 mask protects your lungs from inhaling harmful volcanic ash when Taal Volcano in Batangas erupts.
Swimming at beaches facing the West Philippine Sea requires caution because strong rip currents can pull swimmers out to sea.
Drinking only boiled or bottled water in remote provinces like Mountain Province prevents severe stomach infections from contaminated natural springs.
